signal.note: Shapes only — dot, ring, underline, focus outline, caret, selection tint. 2.65:1 on the light ground, so never text.

signal-ink.dark: var(--signal) — aliased; the deep ground already clears contrast
signal-ink.note: Text-only sibling of the accent, 4.92:1 on the light ground. Carries the finale phrase and arrow-link hover.

ground.note: The page. Painted on body and on the fixed wash behind everything.

ink.note: All primary text and every icon stroke. 4.94:1 on the light ground, 5.52:1 over glass.

ink-2.note: Ledes, taglines, bullets, captions, footer. Darkened one step on 2026-09-02 when the light glass was thinned, so body runs over 0.40-alpha glass still clear 4.5:1 on the composited ground; the dark value runs brighter than a conventional muted tone because it sits over lit blobs.

surface.note: The shadcn --card / --popover / --sidebar slot. Rare in this world; the frosted glass tokens do the work instead.

glass.note: Rest fill for every floating panel: cards, timeline cards, flow nodes and bus. Thinned from 0.52 on 2026-09-02 so the light cards read as glass rather than paper. Alpha over the wash; the value only means anything with backdrop-filter behind it.

glass-strong.note: Hover fill for cards; rest fill for the case-study header panel, the card media frame, the shell's menu pill, the theme toggle and the scroll ring.

glass-raised.note: An object ON glass: every pill (.pill, .live-link, .tech__item, the timeline project chip, flow branch tags). Glass on glass disappears; this rung is what keeps a control visible inside a panel.

glass-edge.note: The 1px border that declares elevation. This system's entire depth vocabulary.

spot-core.note: Stop 1 of the pointer spotlight (.wash__spot), a 420px circle. It lives inside the fixed wash, under everything, so it is ground and takes blob colour: The Ground-Only Iridescence Rule holds. In dark the stops are ordered by luminance, not alpha: a 0.1 core under a 24% blue measured dimmer than its own ring (0.032 against 0.047) and the light rendered as a donut.

spot-hue.canonical: color-mix(in oklab, color-mix(in oklab, var(--blob-c-2) 50%, white) 36%, transparent)
spot-hue.note: Stop 2 of the spotlight, at 15%. In light the blob hue is pulled 50% toward white first, so the light lightens the ground under text rather than saturating it.

spot-hue-2.canonical: color-mix(in oklab, color-mix(in oklab, var(--blob-a-2) 50%, white) 22%, transparent)
spot-hue-2.note: Stop 3 of the spotlight, at 32%, repeated at 35% strength at 58% before transparent. Five stops, not three: evenly spaced stops read as rings and the eye finds the outer edge; the tail, still long in proportion, is what keeps it a glow. The stops are weighted inward so the bright part of the light is a point rather than a disc.

card-glow.note: The soft light that follows the pointer across frosted glass: a 380px circle on .card::after, 300px on .flow__node::after, centred on --mx/--my and fading to transparent at 62%. A gloss on the glass, never a colour.

blob-gloss.note: Radial highlight at 34%/28%, r 46%, clipped to each blob path. A radial gradient on purpose — same look as a blurred spot, no filter pass. Fades to --blob-gloss-out, rgb(255 255 255 / 0), in both themes.

blob-a-1.note: Top-left blob, stop 1 of 3. Gradient axis 8% 0% → 92% 100%.

blob-a-2.note: Top-left blob, stop 2. Also the third stop of the card gradient edge.

blob-b-1.note: Top-right blob, stop 1. Also the middle stop of the card gradient edge.

blob-c-1.note: Bottom-left blob, stop 1. Also the first stop of the card gradient edge. Gradient axis 0% 20% → 100% 80%.

display.purpose: The hero headline only, uppercase Unbounded at 700. Carries the outline-and-fill device: .type-outline renders solid ink by default and switches to color: transparent with -webkit-text-stroke: 0.03em at font-weight 400 inside an @supports guard, because Unbounded's heavy weights self-overlap and stroke into visible construction lines. Stroke floors at max(1.1px, 0.03em) under 720px. Drops to clamp(1.25rem, 5.9vw, 1.875rem) / line-height 1.18 under 720px.

headline.purpose: Section titles — WORK, STACK, ABOUT — uppercase. Contact overrides to clamp(2.25rem, 6.5vw, 4.5rem); the menu's section links run clamp(1.75rem, 5vw, 2.5rem).

title.purpose: Project card names, uppercase. The flagship card scales to clamp(1.625rem, 3vw, 2.5rem).

body.purpose: Every paragraph, in Hanken Grotesk at 17px. Measures capped: 46ch hero subline, 42ch section ledes, 40ch card taglines and contact lede, 52ch flagship description, 60ch About (line-height 1.6).

label.purpose: Captions, flow details, the footer and the mobile tech name, at normal tracking in sentence case. The tracked-caps 0.06em variant of this step belonged to the hero's status line and was removed with it on 2026-09-03; the tracked caps that remain (the menu keycap and .pending-note) sit smaller and at 0.08em.

micro-label.purpose: The last tracked-caps step: 600 / 0.75rem / 0.08em uppercase on the menu keycaps and the "coming soon" pending flag; the same size at 700 in the display face numbers the flow diagram's nodes. The 0.6875rem step below it carried the project card's taxonomy label (.card__label) and nothing else, and went with the label on 2026-09-03. No .pill carries tracking or uppercase any more.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The default. Every hover, press, fade, rise and swap. The built-in keywords are too weak.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Symmetric moves. ease-in on its own is banned.

motion.name: ease-drawer
motion.purpose: The menu sheet's slide, applied through shadcn's Sheet content class.

motion.name: duration-press
motion.purpose: transform on :active { scale(0.97) }, on every pressable element.

motion.name: duration-hover
motion.purpose: Colour, background, border-color and icon nudges.

motion.name: duration-roll-in
motion.purpose: Rolling phrase entrance from translateY(0.7em) + blur(3px). Must match ROLL_MS in RoleRoll.tsx.

motion.name: duration-roll-out
motion.purpose: Rolling phrase exit to translateY(-0.85em). Exits are faster than entrances.

motion.name: duration-reveal
motion.purpose: Scroll-in rise for below-the-fold blocks, 24px of travel, staggered 50ms per sibling.

motion.name: drift
motion.purpose: Ambient blob drift, 5-7vmax translate and 7-11deg rotation. Disabled under 720px and under reduced motion.

motion.name: duration-card-transform
motion.purpose: The card's one composed transform: perspective(1100px) translateY(--lift) rotateX(--rx) rotateY(--ry) scale(--press). Hover sets --lift: -6px, TiltCard.tsx writes --rx/--ry, :active sets --press: 0.98 and shortens the transition to 160ms. Retargeted on every pointer move so the tilt trails the pointer instead of snapping to it. The card mark's translate(-6px, -6px) scale(1.05) and opacity 0.72 to 1 run at the same 320ms.

motion.name: tilt
motion.purpose: Peak card tilt at an edge, as --rx/--ry from TiltCard.tsx; the top or right edge tips away so the card leans toward the hand. Mouse only, fine pointer only; dropped under reduced motion while the highlight stays. Flow nodes take the highlight but never the tilt: their connectors are pseudo-elements aligned to the node edges, so a rotated node pulls its edge off the arrow pointing at it.

motion.name: duration-card-glow
motion.purpose: Opacity of the specular highlight (.card::after at 380px, .flow__node::after at 300px): a circle of --card-glow at --mx/--my fading to transparent at 62%, z-index -1 inside the surface's own backdrop-filter stacking context, so it sits above the frosted fill and below every child. Position is written by TiltCard.tsx and FlowGlow.tsx; only opacity transitions. On leave --mx/--my are left where they were, so the light fades out in place rather than jumping to centre.

motion.name: spotlight-spring
motion.purpose: The pointer spotlight (.wash__spot, Spotlight.tsx): omega ~17.3 rad/s, zeta ~0.90, just under critical, no visible overshoot. Time constant ~64ms, so it covers 95% of any distance in about 190ms and then runs on while the invisible remainder decays under the rest threshold (measured 420ms to rest after 60px, 530ms after 800px). Semi-implicit Euler, dt clamped to 32ms so a waking tab does not fling the light across the screen; the loop stops at rest (0.15px, 2px/s), which is what keeps it out of the ambient budget. translate3d written directly on the element, never a custom property on an ancestor.

motion.name: duration-spotlight
motion.purpose: Opacity of .wash__spot via [data-on]. It appears where the pointer first is rather than flying in from a corner. Hidden on window blur, on a hidden tab and when the pointer leaves the window; never mounted without a fine pointer or under reduced motion.

motion.name: duration-underline
motion.purpose: The 2px --signal rule under .link-arrow and .case__back: scaleX(0) to scaleX(1) with transform-origin left on hover, exiting with transform-origin right, so the line sweeps through rather than retreating the way it came. transform only. Never drawn on .is-pending, which is not a control. The Experience timeline's project chip is excluded: it is a bordered pill and takes a coral border instead, because a rule drawn inside a pill reads as a slip. The arrow moves 6px alongside it, the one nudge distance in the system.

motion.name: recede
motion.purpose: The scroll handoff at the top of each route: opacity to 0, scale to 0.9, translate to 0 22%, filter blur to --recede-blur (10px above 760px, 0px below), transform-origin 50% 45%, linear, view() timeline. Finished state is the default, so a refresh mid-page renders the right frame with no flash and no JS. Runs on the 404's headline panel too. ScrollScrub.tsx mirrors these frames through WAAPI on [data-scrub] elements where animation-timeline is missing; change both together.

motion.name: card-unveil
motion.purpose: The other half of the handoff: clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0 round --radius-card) to inset(0 0 80% 0) at 50% to inset(0 0 0 0), scale 0.96 to 1, opacity 0.5 to 0.85 to 1, linear, view() timeline. It lags the viewport edge then catches up, so the card is seen being drawn rather than merely arriving. The flagship's Reveal is neutralised inside the guard so one element has one entrance.

Since 2026-09-03 it is a two-column grid: the head spans both columns, the body and the foot stack in the text column, and the mark sits beside them.

narrative.overview:
A person who is several things at once, introducing himself on a sheet of iridescent film. The ground is a cool lavender-grey with four soft gradient blobs pushed hard into the corners and a real film-grain tile over everything; the centre of the viewport stays calm so wide display capitals can sit on it without fighting colour. The page's whole argument is made twice, once by the words and once by the material: the blobs are three-stop gradients on four different axes, so nothing repeats, and the frosted cards that float over them borrow their colour rather than adding a new one.

Density is low and deliberate. One 1140px column, generous vertical air (80px in, 96px out per section), an 18px grid gap, and long unbroken measures (40–46ch on ledes, 60ch on About). The register is adult and editorial, never bubbly: no sparkles, no candy pastels, no 40px pillow corners, no glossy mascot shapes. Colour lives in the ground; the foreground is ink, glass and one coral.

Two complete themes ship. Dark is not an inverted filter. It is a second token set with a deep indigo ground, a second full set of blob stops mixed brighter, and the blobs held to 62% opacity so body text still survives over them. Every visual decision is expressed as a custom property in app/globals.css, which is the normative source for both.
keyCharacteristics: Iridescent gradient blobs in all four corners, calm ground in the middle
Wide uppercase display capitals with an outline-and-fill contrast device
Frosted glass surfaces whose blur is legibility, not decoration
Glass on every pill, control and panel; the only opaque surface is the screenshot well
Exactly one accent colour, split into a shape token and a text token
A real 128px grain raster, not an SVG filter
Flat by construction: edges and blur convey depth, never shadows

rules.name: The Two Corals Rule
rules.body: --signal draws shapes; --signal-ink writes words. Never swap them. The light accent fails text contrast (2.65:1) and the dark ground makes a second value unnecessary, which is exactly why the split is a token and not a judgement call.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Coral appears in eight KINDS of place and no more: the finale phrase, the live dot, the email underline, the scroll-ring fill, the focus outline, the caret/selection tint, the arrow-link hover tint, and the hover edge tint.

rules.name: The Calm Centre Rule
rules.body: Iridescence lives in the four corners at negative offsets; the middle band of every viewport stays ground. Type is never composited over a gradient peak, which is what lets 4.9:1 ink hold on a coloured page.

rules.name: The Ground-Only Iridescence Rule
rules.body: Blob colours are for the wash and for the two gradient lines (card edge, timeline rail). They never become body text, a surface background, or a control fill. The one amendment (2026-09-03): the live-link wears the gradient at rest, as a 1.5px ring of --gh-hue-1 to --gh-hue-3 on its edge and a translucent wash of the same hues over its raised glass, at half opacity at rest and full on hover. Blob-derived colour on a control's edge and over its surface, allowed the way the card edge and the hovered GitHub mark are: a line and a tint, never a text colour and never a solid fill.

rules.name: The Outline-Lead Rule
rules.body: Only the lead-in words are outlined: "HEY, I'M". The subject is always filled. Outline is a contrast device between the greeting and the person, never a decoration applied to a whole heading.

rules.name: The Never-Stroke-Bold Rule
rules.body: Outlined type runs at weight 400 inside the @supports guard, and the solid fallback runs at 700. Raising the outline weight to match the fill re-introduces the self-overlap artefacts the guard exists to avoid.

rules.name: The Uppercase Display Rule
rules.body: h1, h2 and h3 are uppercase Unbounded at 700 with positive tracking (0.015em base). Body copy is never uppercase; only the two micro steps and the timeline period are, and they always carry at least 0.02em tracking (0.06em and up below 15px) to stay legible.

rules.name: The 1140 Rule
rules.body: Content lives in a 1140px column with the gutter outside it: max-width: calc(1140px + var(--gutter) * 2) with padding: … var(--gutter). Writing it as max-width: 1140px with border-box padding yields a 1092px column and quietly contradicts the rule. The only full-bleed layers are the fixed wash and the fixed header.

rules.name: The Fixed-Ground Rule
rules.body: The wash is position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: -1, aria-hidden, and pointer-events: none. It scrolls with nothing and intercepts nothing.

rules.name: The Portrait-vmax Rule
rules.body: Blobs are sized in vmax on desktop (40 to 46vmax) but in vw under 720px (76 to 84vw), because on a phone vmax is the viewport *height*, which makes the blobs full-bleed and swallows the body copy.

rules.name: The Edge-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface declares its elevation once, as an edge. A 1px border *under* a soft drop shadow is the ghost-card look this world refuses. The scroll ring is the one glass object that carries no edge (border: 0); it is a control on the page, not a panel on the wash.

rules.name: The Blur-Is-Legibility Rule
rules.body: Any surface that carries text over the wash must carry backdrop-filter: blur() saturate(). The blur is what keeps text readable over a saturated blob; it is a functional requirement, not a finish.

rules.name: The Held-Back-Blob Rule
rules.body: In dark, .wash__blob runs at opacity: 0.62. The blobs are far brighter than the deep indigo ground, and body text has to survive over them.

rules.name: The One Radius Family Rule
rules.body: 22px panel, 999px pill, 1rem control, 0.6rem branch, 6px keycap, 4px focus. A new value needs a new reason.

rules.name: The Drawn-Not-Set Rule
rules.body: Every mark on this page is authored SVG in currentColor: the monogram, the three-rule menu glyph, the arrows, the sun and moon, the seven project marks, the case-study bullet and the flow arrowheads. No icon fonts, no glyph characters standing in for icons, no raster illustration.

rules.name: The Glass Ladder Rule
rules.body: Four opacities and no fifth: --glass rest, --glass-strong lit, --glass-raised for an object on glass, --glass-edge for the line. A surface picks its rung by what it sits on, not by taste: a pill inside a card takes raised because glass on glass disappears. There is no color-mix of white into anything; the ladder is the whole vocabulary.

rules.name: The Tracked-Caps-In-The-Foot Rule
rules.body: Retired 2026-09-03. It used to read: the .pill carries no tracking and no uppercase by default, and .card__label adds both because a card foot is the only place the system allows tracked caps as a label. The label came off the card, so the exception has no user and the rule is now simply its first clause: no .pill carries tracking or uppercase. About's range and the footer line are sentence case at 500. The tracked caps that survive, the menu keycap and the pending flag, are neither .pills nor in a card foot, and the card foot is now the card's last line.

rules.name: The Live-Link Rule
rules.body: A project with a public, working deployment gets a demo, and that link is the loudest affordance on its card and repeats at the TOP of its case study, not only in the footer. A thing a visitor can *use* outranks a thing they can read. It renders as a raised glass pill (.live-link: {colors.glass-raised} behind blur(12px), 999px, padding 13px 20px 13px 17px, 1rem at 600, line-height 1.25, 10px gap) carrying a static 9px coral dot with a 3px halo ring (--signal at 26%), the text "Try it live" on the card and "Try {name} live" on the case study, and a trailing ArrowUpRight. Restyled 2026-09-03: it is the one pill that wears the world's colour at rest. Its 1px border is a transparent spacer; the edge is a 1.5px ring on ::before (linear-gradient 120deg of --gh-hue-1, --gh-hue-2, --gh-hue-3, padding-box masked like .card::before) and a ::after wash of the same hues (color-mix 22% / 16% / 22% into transparent) sits at opacity 0.5. Hover brings the wash to full, swells the dot to 1.35 and moves the arrow translate(3px, -3px); the 2px lift alone is gated behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference. No coral edge tint any more. Press scales 0.97. The case-study instance (.case__live) sits 22px under the title, before every other fact. This system has no buttons; the pill is the strongest control shape it owns.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: CaseStudySection takes exactly { id, title, children }. There is no label, kicker, eyebrow, number or index prop and none may be added. The eyebrow above a heading is the one ban no brief earns back, and the section sequence carries no information the reader needs; the headings do. Making the slot structurally unavailable is stronger than leaving it unused.

dos: Do put every new colour through the token layer in app/globals.css, and define it in both :root and .dark. A value that only exists in one theme is a bug.
Do use --signal for marks and --signal-ink for text (The Two Corals Rule).

Do build every new surface from the glass ladder: --glass for a panel, --glass-strong for a lit or heavy one, --glass-raised for a pill or control sitting on glass, always with a 1px --glass-edge and a backdrop-filter matched to its size.
Do reach for .pill before inventing a small surface; it is the range chip, the footer line and the base shape for every small control.

Do keep new sections inside .section (a 1140px column with var(--gutter) outside it, 80px to 96px vertical) and give them an id plus aria-labelledby, so the menu and the number shortcuts can reach them.
Do wrap below-the-fold content in <Reveal> and stagger siblings at 50 to 70ms; drive any choreography inside it off data-reveal with transitions, the way the timeline and the flow do.
Do author new icons as SVG in currentColor at the established stroke weights (2.25 for UI arrows, 2.5 for project marks), round caps and joins.

Do put every hover rule behind @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) and give every pressable a :active { scale(0.97) }, 0.98 on large surfaces, and outside the hover guard, since touch devices have no hover state.

Do drive any new state on .card through --lift or --press, and any new state on the menu link, the live-link or the repo button through their own --shift / --lift / --press, rather than a second transform declaration (The One Composed Transform Rule).

Do make pointer-driven and scroll-driven motion stop when the user does: a loop tests for rest and cancels its frame, a scrub defaults to its finished state, and the resting page is complete (The User-Is-The-Clock Rule).

Do ship blocked content by ABSENCE. An unwritten case-study section does not render, tech: [] renders no row, media: [] renders no band. Never a placeholder, a skeleton or "coming soon" on a case study.
Do put text that sits outside the calm band on a surface rather than trying to move it (The Surface-Not-Spacing Rule).
Do write copy with commas, colons, periods, middle dots and hyphens. There are no em dashes anywhere in user-visible text.
Do regenerate the grain with node scripts/make-grain.mjs public/textures/grain.png rather than hand-editing the PNG; the seed is the provenance.
Do cap measures: 40 to 46ch for ledes and taglines, 52 to 62ch for bullets and notes, 60ch for long-form body.
Do keep the outline device on lead-in words only, at weight 400 inside the @supports guard.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow. This system has none; elevation is an edge over blur (The Edge-Not-Shadow Rule).

Don't paint blob colours onto text or use them as a solid fill. They are ground and the gradient line: the card edge, the timeline rail, the hovered GitHub mark and, since 2026-09-03, the live-link's 1.5px ring and its translucent wash (The Ground-Only Iridescence Rule and its one amendment).
Don't mix white into a surface by hand or add a fifth glass opacity; the ladder is the whole vocabulary (The Glass Ladder Rule).
Don't stroke display type at 700; Unbounded's heavy contours self-overlap and the stroke exposes the construction lines.
Don't size the blobs in vmax below 720px; portrait vmax is the viewport height and the blobs swallow the copy.
Don't animate anything interruptible with a keyframe. Use a transition so it can retarget mid-flight.
Don't let a stagger exceed 80ms per step, or an exit run longer than its entrance.
Don't animate a keyboard-initiated scroll, and don't put scroll-behavior: smooth outside the reduced-motion guard.

Don't give ScrollScrub.tsx a second range or a second keyframe set. It mirrors @keyframes recede and nothing else; a change to either is a change to both, and anything wider is the polyfill this system refuses.
Don't tilt a card or show the spotlight for a touch or pen pointer, or under reduced motion (the highlight may stay; the tilt and the light may not).
Don't draw the arrow underline inside a bordered pill. It belongs on unbounded links (.link-arrow, .case__back); a pill takes a coral border instead.

Don't add a third continuous ambient motion; two families (the blob drift, the caret blink) is the budget, and it shrank from three on 2026-09-03 rather than leaving a vacancy. A second live indicator stays static.
Don't bring the Stack section or its orbit back. Tools appear only on the case study where they were used, as tiles, and data/stack.ts has exactly that one consumer.
Don't ship a dead link. An unavailable action takes the designed pending state (.is-pending plus a .pending-note pill), inert to pointer, keyboard and screen reader.
Don't introduce a seventh radius, a second accent, or a new display face.

Don't put tracked caps on a .pill. Every pill is sentence case at 500; the only tracked caps left are the menu keycap and the pending flag, and the card foot carries none (The Tracked-Caps-In-The-Foot Rule, retired).
Don't animate transform: from a scroll timeline. Scroll gets translate:/scale:; interaction keeps transform:, or the scroll animation silently eats the hover.
Don't put a :active transform on an element that owns a full-card overlay pseudo-element; it drags the overlay out from under the cursor and the card stops being clickable (The Card-As-Link Rule).
Don't infer a tool→project mapping, a role, a date, or a metric. If it was not supplied, the field stays empty and the UI omits it.
Don't add a label, kicker, eyebrow or number prop to CaseStudySection, and don't add a standfirst or a description paragraph back to the header or the card.
Don't give Operations Agent a repo affordance of any kind, including a disabled one.
Don't render a shadcn Badge; the .pill class is the badge.
Don't override shadcn's --accent expecting the page accent; that slot belongs to shadcn, ours is --signal.
